property_summary: For every call to fallback with any sender and amount, the reference C accepts and updates pastBlockTime exactly when msg.value == 10 ether (i.e. calls with value == 10 ether succeed and update pastBlockTime), whereas the mutant rejects or accepts a different set of msg.value (5 ether) and thus there exist inputs where the mutant's acceptance/update behavior differs from the reference.

For any caller and ether amount, the reference contract's fallback accepts and updates pastBlockTime exactly when msg.value == 10 ether (so calls with 10 ether succeed and set pastBlockTime > previous), while the mutant accepts a different value (5 ether) and thus will refuse or accept different calls — the property asserts that a call with value 10 ether always succeeds and increases pastBlockTime.

For every caller and timestamp, calling the contract's payable fallback with exactly 10 ether must succeed and advance pastBlockTime (make it strictly greater than its previous value); the mutant that requires 5 ether will reject some of those 10-ether calls and thus violate this rule.

The reference contract C enforces strictly increasing pastBlockTime on every fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether (block.timestamp > pastBlockTime), while the mutant allows equal timestamps (>=) so it can leave pastBlockTime unchanged across two calls with the same block.timestamp and thus violate the strictly-increasing-time property.

For any caller and any timestamp, after a successful fallback call sending exactly 10 ether the contract's pastBlockTime strictly increases (new pastBlockTime > old pastBlockTime); the mutant that uses >= can allow pastBlockTime to remain equal when two calls occur with the same block.timestamp, violating strict increase.

For any successful call to fallback sending exactly 10 ether, C always updates pastBlockTime to a strictly larger value than before (new > old); the mutant allowing >= can leave pastBlockTime unchanged when two calls occur in the same block, breaking strict increase.

For any successful fallback call sending exactly 10 ether, the contract's public pastBlockTime strictly increases (new pastBlockTime > old pastBlockTime); the mutant that uses >= can allow pastBlockTime to remain equal when two calls happen in the same block, violating strict increase.

For any successful fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether, the contract's public pastBlockTime strictly increases (new > old); the mutant using >= allows pastBlockTime to stay equal for calls in the same block, violating strict increase.

For any caller and timestamp where fallback is called with exactly 10 ether and block.timestamp strictly greater than prior pastBlockTime, the reference contract always updates pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp (so getter pastBlockTime equals block.timestamp after the call); the mutant that stores block.number instead can make pastBlockTime != block.timestamp for some inputs (timestamps/blocks) and thus violates this invariant.
